sentences.text:
Heard Sri Satya Prakash learned counsel for the applicant; Sri Pankaj Kumar Mishra, learned
counsel for the informant; learned Aga for the State and perused the material placed on record.

2.  The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant, Nishant Pandit with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 252 of 2024, under Sections 376, 384, 506 IPC and 67 Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Harduaganj, District- Aligarh,
during pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The allegations in the F.I.R. are that the informant is employed as Associate Professor in Aligarh Ayurvedic Medical College.
She has alleged that the applicant was having relationship with the informant for last 3 years.
When she severed her relationship with him he made her nude photo vides viral on Whats app of all the persons known to her.
He is pressurizing her to commit suicide.
4. The learned counsel for the applicant submits that he never loaded any photo of the victim on social media nor made if viral.

Rather the victim has some nude photographs with the applicant on the basis of which she was blackmailing the applicant to bear her expenses otherwise she will falsely implicate him in case under Section 376 I.P.C. and 67 of Information Technology Act.
The victim had three years relationship with the applicant and thereafter she has lodged the F.I.R. against the applicant.

The applicant is in jail since 17.08.2024.
5.

The counsel for the informant has vehemently approached the bail application and has submitted that the victim has provided the photo and video made by the applicant viral in compact device to the police along with her certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act
During investigation, the victim provided the account statement of transfer of Rs.1,80,800/-to the applicant in his PAYTM Account 6.
The learned A.G.A. has also opposed the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. After hearing rival submissions this court finds that the offence of rape alleged against the applicant does not seems probable since earlier victim had consenting relationship with the applicant for last 3 years.
In this period of 3 years she has transferred money to the PAYTM account of the applicant when their relationship were cordial.
Therefore, the allegation of extortion against the applicant does not appears to the correct.

The allegation of commission of offence of criminal intimidation appears to have been made only to lend further colour to the case No evidence of commission of offence under Section-67 of I.T. Act is proved since only the victim has provided the photographs and videos in her possession recorded in compact device by her.
She has not informed the names and mobile numbers of the persons on whose WhatsApp accounts, her nude photographs and video were made viral by the applicant.

8. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence on record regarding complicity of the accused,
submissions of the learned counsel for the parties noted herein above, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant, Nishant Pandit involved in Case Crime No. 252 of 2024, under Sections 376,
384, 506 IPC and 67 Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Harduaganj,
District- Aligarh be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

Further,
before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or as directed by the Court.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) In case the applicant misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the complainant is free to move an application for cancellation of bail before this court.
11. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
